type: string required: true default: none applicability: cli excerpt: | When Claude should delegate to this subagent caveats: - "Claude automatically delegates tasks based on the task description in your request, the `description` field in subagent configurations, and current context" - "To encourage proactive delegation, include phrases like 'use proactively' in your subagent's description field" notes_for_skill: - "primary delegation signal — the most important field for influencing when Claude uses this subagent" - "should describe circumstances for use, not just what the subagent does" source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents section: "Supported frontmatter fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: list required: false default: "inherits all tools from main conversation" applicability: cli excerpt: | [Tools] the subagent can use. Inherits all tools if omitted
To restrict tools, use either the `tools` field (allowlist) or the `disallowedTools` field (denylist). This example uses `tools` to exclusively allow Read, Grep, Glob, and Bash. The subagent can't edit files, write files, or use any MCP tools:
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
If both are set, `disallowedTools` is applied first, then `tools` is resolved against the remaining pool. A tool listed in both is removed.
When an agent runs as the main thread with `claude --agent`, it can spawn subagents using the Agent tool. To restrict which subagent types it can spawn, use `Agent(agent_type)` syntax in the `tools` field.
This is an allowlist: only the `worker` and `researcher` subagents can be spawned. If the agent tries to spawn any other type, the request fails and the agent sees only the allowed types in its prompt. To block specific agents while allowing all others, use `permissions.deny` instead.
To allow spawning any subagent without restrictions, use `Agent` without parentheses.
If `Agent` is omitted from the `tools` list entirely, the agent cannot spawn any subagents. This restriction only applies to agents running as the main thread with `claude --agent`. Subagents cannot spawn other subagents, so `Agent(agent_type)` has no effect in subagent definitions. caveats: - "allowlist: only listed tools are available; all others (including MCP) are blocked" - "`Agent(name)` syntax in tools restricts which subagent types can be spawned — applies only when running as main thread via --agent, has no effect in subagent definitions" - "if both tools and disallowedTools are set, disallowedTools is applied first" - "In version 2.1.63, the Task tool was renamed to Agent. Existing `Task(...)` references still work as aliases" notes_for_skill: - "prefer listing specific tools (allowlist) for security-sensitive subagents; use disallowedTools when you want to inherit most tools but block a few" source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents section: "Supported frontmatter fields; Available tools; Restrict which subagents can be spawned" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: list required: false default: none applicability: cli excerpt: | Tools to deny, removed from inherited or specified list
This example uses `disallowedTools` to inherit every tool from the main conversation except Write and Edit. The subagent keeps Bash, MCP tools, and everything else:
disallowedTools: Write, Edit
If both are set, `disallowedTools` is applied first, then `tools` is resolved against the remaining pool. A tool listed in both is removed. caveats: - "denylist: subagent inherits all tools except those listed" - "if both tools and disallowedTools are set, disallowedTools is applied first" notes_for_skill: - "use when you want to remove a few dangerous tools (e.g. Write, Bash) but keep the rest" source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents section: "Supported frontmatter fields; Available tools" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: string required: false default: inherit values: [sonnet, opus, haiku, "", inherit] applicability: cli excerpt: | [Model] to use: `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, a full model ID (for example, `claude-opus-4-7`), or `inherit`. Defaults to `inherit`
The `model` field controls which AI model the subagent uses: - Model alias: Use one of the available aliases: `sonnet`, `opus`, or `haiku` - Full model ID: Use a full model ID such as `claude-opus-4-7` or `claude-sonnet-4-6`. Accepts the same values as the `--model` flag - inherit: Use the same model as the main conversation - Omitted: If not specified, defaults to `inherit` (uses the same model as the main conversation)
When Claude invokes a subagent, it can also pass a `model` parameter for that specific invocation. Claude Code resolves the subagent's model in this order: 1. The `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` environment variable, if set 2. The per-invocation `model` parameter 3. The subagent definition's `model` frontmatter 4. The main conversation's model caveats: - "4-level resolution hierarchy: env var > per-invocation param > frontmatter > parent model" - "aliases (sonnet, opus, haiku) resolve to the current latest model for that family — may change over time" - "full model IDs pin a specific version and are stable across releases" notes_for_skill: - "use full model ID when you need a specific capability (e.g. claude-opus-4-7 for xhigh effort)" - "use alias when you want the subagent to track the latest model in that family" source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents section: "Supported frontmatter fields; Choose a model" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: enum required: false default: inherits from main conversation values: [default, acceptEdits, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions, plan] applicability: cli excerpt: | [Permission mode]: `default`, `acceptEdits`, `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions`, or `plan`
The `permissionMode` field controls how the subagent handles permission prompts. Subagents inherit the permission context from the main conversation and can override the mode, except when the parent mode takes precedence as described below.
Mode behaviors: - default: Standard permission checking with prompts - acceptEdits: Auto-accept file edits and common filesystem commands for paths in the working directory or `additionalDirectories` - auto: Auto mode: a background classifier reviews commands and protected-directory writes - dontAsk: Auto-deny permission prompts (explicitly allowed tools still work) - bypassPermissions: Skip permission prompts - plan: Plan mode (read-only exploration)
Use `bypassPermissions` with caution. It skips permission prompts, allowing the subagent to execute operations without approval. Writes to `.git`, `.claude`, `.vscode`, `.idea`, and `.husky` directories still prompt for confirmation, except for `.claude/commands`, `.claude/agents`, and `.claude/skills`.
If the parent uses `bypassPermissions`, this takes precedence and cannot be overridden. If the parent uses auto mode, the subagent inherits auto mode and any `permissionMode` in its frontmatter is ignored: the classifier evaluates the subagent's tool calls with the same block and allow rules as the parent session. caveats: - "parent bypassPermissions cannot be overridden by subagent" - "parent auto mode cannot be overridden by subagent — frontmatter permissionMode is ignored" - "bypassPermissions still prompts for writes to .git, .claude, .vscode, .idea, .husky (except .claude/commands, .claude/agents, .claude/skills)" - "plugin subagents do not support this field — it is silently ignored" notes_for_skill: - "use acceptEdits for write-capable subagents that should not prompt; use plan for read-only analysis agents" source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents section: "Supported frontmatter fields; Permission modes" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: integer required: false default: none applicability: cli excerpt: | Maximum number of agentic turns before the subagent stops notes_for_skill: - "useful for bounded research or verification tasks where open-ended looping is undesirable" source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents section: "Supported frontmatter fields" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: list required: false default: none applicability: cli excerpt: | [Skills] to load into the subagent's context at startup. The full skill content is injected, not just made available for invocation. Subagents don't inherit skills from the parent conversation
Use the `skills` field to inject skill content into a subagent's context at startup. This gives the subagent domain knowledge without requiring it to discover and load skills during execution.
The full content of each skill is injected into the subagent's context, not just made available for invocation. Subagents don't inherit skills from the parent conversation; you must list them explicitly.
This is the inverse of running a skill in a subagent. With `skills` in a subagent, the subagent controls the system prompt and loads skill content. With `context: fork` in a skill, the skill content is injected into the agent you specify. Both use the same underlying system. caveats: - "skills are NOT inherited from the parent conversation — must be listed explicitly" - "full skill content is injected at startup (increases context); not lazy-loaded" - "plugin subagents do not support this field — it is silently ignored" notes_for_skill: - "primary injection point for the subagent-builder skill itself: list the skill here to give subagents the skill's guidance at runtime" - "injecting a large skill inflates context from turn 1; only inject skills the subagent will actively use" source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents section: "Supported frontmatter fields; Preload skills into subagents" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: list required: false default: inherits MCP servers from main conversation applicability: cli excerpt: | [MCP servers] available to this subagent. Each entry is either a server name referencing an already-configured server (e.g., `"slack"`) or an inline definition with the server name as key and a full [MCP server config] as value
Use the `mcpServers` field to give a subagent access to MCP servers that aren't available in the main conversation. Inline servers defined here are connected when the subagent starts and disconnected when it finishes. String references share the parent session's connection.
Each entry in the list is either an inline server definition or a string referencing an MCP server already configured in your session.
Inline definitions use the same schema as `.mcp.json` server entries (`stdio`, `http`, `sse`, `ws`), keyed by the server name.
To keep an MCP server out of the main conversation entirely and avoid its tool descriptions consuming context there, define it inline here rather than in `.mcp.json`. The subagent gets the tools; the parent conversation does not. caveats: - "inline definitions: connected at subagent start, disconnected at finish" - "string references: reuse parent session's already-open connection" - "plugin subagents do not support this field — it is silently ignored" - "inline servers keep MCP tool descriptions out of the parent conversation context" notes_for_skill: - "use inline definitions when the MCP server is only relevant to this subagent (keeps parent context clean)" - "use string reference when the server is already configured and shared connections are acceptable" source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents section: "Supported frontmatter fields; Scope MCP servers to a subagent" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: object required: false default: none applicability: cli excerpt: | [Lifecycle hooks] scoped to this subagent
Define hooks directly in the subagent's markdown file. These hooks only run while that specific subagent is active and are cleaned up when it finishes.
Frontmatter hooks fire when the agent is spawned as a subagent through the Agent tool or an @-mention. They do not fire when the agent runs as the main session via `--agent` or the `agent` setting. For session-wide hooks, configure them in `settings.json`.
All hook events are supported. The most common events for subagents are: - PreToolUse (matcher: Tool name): Before the subagent uses a tool - PostToolUse (matcher: Tool name): After the subagent uses a tool - Stop (none): When the subagent finishes (converted to SubagentStop at runtime)
`Stop` hooks in frontmatter are automatically converted to `SubagentStop` events. caveats: - "hooks fire only when spawned via Agent tool or @-mention — NOT when running as main session via --agent" - "Stop hooks in frontmatter are converted to SubagentStop at runtime" - "plugin subagents do not support this field — it is silently ignored" notes_for_skill: - "use PreToolUse hooks to validate or constrain tool calls (e.g., block SQL writes)" - "session-level subagent lifecycle hooks (SubagentStart, SubagentStop) go in settings.json, not here" source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents section: "Supported frontmatter fields; Define hooks for subagents; Hooks in subagent frontmatter" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: enum required: false default: none values: [user, project, local] applicability: cli excerpt: | [Persistent memory scope]: `user`, `project`, or `local`. Enables cross-session learning
The `memory` field gives the subagent a persistent directory that survives across conversations. The subagent uses this directory to build up knowledge over time, such as codebase patterns, debugging insights, and architectural decisions.
Scope options: - user: ~/.claude/agent-memory// — subagent should remember learnings across all projects - project: .claude/agent-memory// — subagent's knowledge is project-specific and shareable via version control - local: .claude/agent-memory-local// — subagent's knowledge is project-specific but should not be checked into version control
When memory is enabled: - The subagent's system prompt includes instructions for reading and writing to the memory directory. - The subagent's system prompt also includes the first 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md in the memory directory, whichever comes first, with instructions to curate MEMORY.md if it exceeds that limit. - Read, Write, and Edit tools are automatically enabled so the subagent can manage its memory files. caveats: - "Read, Write, and Edit tools are automatically enabled when memory is set (even if not listed in tools)" - "MEMORY.md is injected into system prompt on every run — keep it curated to avoid context bloat" - "`project` is the recommended default scope (shareable via version control)" notes_for_skill: - "use for subagents that learn and improve over time (code reviewers, domain experts)" source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents section: "Supported frontmatter fields; Enable persistent memory" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00

type: boolean required: false default: false values: [true, false] applicability: cli excerpt: | Set to `true` to always run this subagent as a [background task]. Default: `false`
Background subagents run concurrently while you continue working. Before launching, Claude Code prompts for any tool permissions the subagent will need, ensuring it has the necessary approvals upfront. Once running, the subagent inherits these permissions and auto-denies anything not pre-approved. If a background subagent needs to ask clarifying questions, that tool call fails but the subagent continues. caveats: - "tool permission prompts are shown upfront (before launch), not during execution" - "background subagents auto-deny any tool call not pre-approved at launch time" - "clarifying question tool calls fail silently — background subagents cannot pause for input" notes_for_skill: - "use for fire-and-forget tasks (linting, test runs, research) where you don't need to interact mid-run" source: url: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents section: "Supported frontmatter fields; Run subagents in foreground or background" fetched_at: 2026-04-16T10:15:00-04:00
